format: Text with inline TeX in $...$ and display TeX in $$...$$. Answer label and value fields are TeX without delimiters.

problems.title: Force on a moving charge
problems.prompt: A $2\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ charge moves with $\mathbf{u}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,3\times10^5\ \mathrm{m/s}$ through $\mathbf{B}=\hat{\mathbf{z}}\,0.5\ \mathrm{T}$. Find the force on it.

problems.title: Force on a current-carrying wire
problems.prompt: A $2\ \mathrm{m}$ straight wire along $+\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ carries $5\ \mathrm{A}$ in a uniform field $\mathbf{B}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,0.2\ \mathrm{T}$. Find the force on the wire.

problems.title: Field of a long wire
problems.prompt: A long straight wire carries $10\ \mathrm{A}$. Find $H$ and $B$ in air $5\ \mathrm{cm}$ from it, and compare $B$ with Earth's field of about $50\ \mu\mathrm{T}$.
steps: That is 80.0% of Earth's field, enough to deflect a compass.

problems.title: Finite wire segment
problems.prompt: A straight wire $1\ \mathrm{m}$ long carries $2\ \mathrm{A}$. Find $H$ at a point $20\ \mathrm{cm}$ from its midpoint, on the perpendicular bisector. How much does treating it as infinitely long overestimate the field?
steps: The infinite-wire formula is 7.70% too high here.

problems.title: Circular loop: center and axis
problems.prompt: A loop of radius $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ carries $3\ \mathrm{A}$. Find $H$ at its center and on its axis $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ away.
hints: On the axis the radial parts of $d\mathbf{H}$ cancel; only $H_z$ remains.
steps: At $z=a$ the field is $1/2^{3/2}=0.354$ of its value at the center.

problems.title: Square loop at its center
problems.prompt: A square loop $20\ \mathrm{cm}$ on a side carries $1\ \mathrm{A}$. Find $H$ at its center, and compare with a circular loop of the same perimeter.
hints: Add four finite segments. Each is $d=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the center and runs from $-d$ to $d$ along its length.

problems.title: Long solenoid
problems.prompt: A $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ solenoid has $500$ turns and carries $2\ \mathrm{A}$. Find $H$ and $B$ inside with an air core, and $B$ with an iron core of $\mu_r=200$.

problems.title: Ampère's law in a coax
problems.prompt: A coax has a solid inner conductor of radius $1\ \mathrm{mm}$ carrying $5\ \mathrm{A}$ (spread uniformly) and a thin outer conductor at $4\ \mathrm{mm}$ carrying the $5\ \mathrm{A}$ return. Find $H$ at $r=0.5\ \mathrm{mm}$, $3\ \mathrm{mm}$ and $6\ \mathrm{mm}$.
hints: Inside the inner conductor $I_{\mathrm{enc}}=I\,r^2/a^2$. Outside everything, the currents cancel.
steps: A coax keeps its magnetic field inside, which is why it doesn't radiate or pick up interference.

problems.title: Toroid
problems.prompt: A toroid has $200$ turns carrying $1\ \mathrm{A}$. Find $H$ inside the core at a mean radius of $5\ \mathrm{cm}$, and outside it.
hints: A circle inside the core links the current $NI$; one outside links zero net current.
steps: Outside, a loop links each turn twice (going up and coming down), so $I_{\mathrm{enc}}=0$ and $H=0$.

problems.title: Force between parallel wires
problems.prompt: Two long parallel wires $5\ \mathrm{cm}$ apart carry $10\ \mathrm{A}$ and $20\ \mathrm{A}$ in the same direction. Find the force per meter and whether it attracts or repels.
hints: Wire 1 makes $B_1=\mu_0I_1/(2\pi d)$ at wire 2; the force per meter is $I_2B_1$.
steps: Currents in the same direction attract.

problems.title: Inductance and energy of a solenoid
problems.prompt: A $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ air-core solenoid has $500$ turns and a radius of $1\ \mathrm{cm}$. Find its inductance and the energy stored at $2\ \mathrm{A}$.

problems.title: Flux leaving an iron surface
problems.prompt: Iron ($\mu_r=1000$) fills $z<0$ and air fills $z>0$, with no surface current. In the iron, $\mathbf{B}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,1.2+\hat{\mathbf{z}}\,0.4\ \mathrm{T}$. Find $\mathbf{B}$ in the air just above the surface and the angles from the normal.
steps: The flux leaves the iron almost exactly normal to its surface.

problems.title: Can this be a magnetic field?
problems.prompt: For what value of $k$ is $\mathbf{B}=\hat{\mathbf{x}}\,2x-\hat{\mathbf{y}}\,y+\hat{\mathbf{z}}\,kz$ a possible magnetic field?

problems.title: Flux through a tilted loop
problems.prompt: A circular loop of radius $5\ \mathrm{cm}$ sits in a uniform $\mathbf{B}=\hat{\mathbf{z}}\,0.2\ \mathrm{T}$, with its normal tilted $30^\circ$ from $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$. Find the flux through it.
hints: For a flat loop in a uniform field, $\Phi=BA\cos\theta$.
